stem: Draw the graphs representing the equations \(2x = y + 2\) and \(4x + 3y = 24\) on the same graph paper. Find the area of the triangle formed by these lines and the X-axis.
solution:
Line 1: \(2x = y + 2 \Rightarrow y = 2x - 2\); its X-intercept (\(y = 0\)) is \((1, 0)\).
Line 2: \(4x + 3y = 24\); its X-intercept (\(y = 0\)) is \((6, 0)\).
Point of intersection of the two lines: substitute \(y = 2x - 2\) in \(4x + 3y = 24\): \(4x + 3(2x - 2) = 24 \Rightarrow 4x + 6x - 6 = 24 \Rightarrow 10x = 30 \Rightarrow x = 3\), \(y = 2(3) - 2 = 4\). So they meet at \((3, 4)\).
The triangle formed with the X-axis has vertices \((1, 0)\), \((6, 0)\) and \((3, 4)\). Base \(= 6 - 1 = 5\) units on the X-axis, height \(= 4\) units. Area \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 = 10\) square units.

stem:
The following pie-diagram shows percentage of persons according to blood group in a blood group checking camp. Answer the following questions:
(a) Find the measure of central angle for each blood group.
(b) Find the total number of persons, if there are 600 persons of blood group B.
solution:
From the pie-diagram, the percentages are O = 45%, A = 20%, B = 30%, AB = 5%.
(a) Central angle \(= \dfrac{\text{percentage}}{100} \times 360^\circ\).
Blood group O: \(\dfrac{45}{100} \times 360 = 162^\circ\).
Blood group A: \(\dfrac{20}{100} \times 360 = 72^\circ\).
Blood group B: \(\dfrac{30}{100} \times 360 = 108^\circ\).
Blood group AB: \(\dfrac{5}{100} \times 360 = 18^\circ\).
(b) Blood group B is 30% of the total. If \(30\%\) of the total \(= 600\), then total \(= \dfrac{600 \times 100}{30} = 2000\) persons.
figureNote: Pie chart of blood groups with sectors labelled O = 45%, A = 20%, B = 30%, AB = 5%; p-10
